sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance can ever exist, and it is created lazily the first time it is referenced.
sketches.resonance: Loneliness is not constructed; it simply comes into being the moment you look for it, and there can only ever be one.

sketches.mechanism: A `weak` reference does not keep the referenced object alive; it automatically becomes `nil` when the object is deallocated, requiring optional unwrapping to access.
sketches.resonance: You held someone weakly, so when they left, your reference to them quietly became nothing — and every attempt to reach them now demands you first accept they might be gone.

sketches.mechanism: In Haskell, `fix` computes the fixed point of a function — a value defined entirely in terms of itself, enabling infinite self-reference that only resolves through laziness.
sketches.resonance: Grief is a feeling that produces itself from itself; it only survives because we never evaluate it all at once.
